x: The Poly, however, had first two in the 220 yards, with Badelow and Carmen and then, with their help, they managed to win the 1 Mile Relay. Frank Webb ran very well for us in this, and Henderson, of the Poly, only beat him by a yard or so, over the half-mile stage.
At the end of the first lap (6½ miles) the leaders were Wilson (Sheffield), Henderson (Worthing), Collier (L. Vid.), Christie-Murray (S.W.C.), Tommy Green (Bel.), followed by Plumb (Enfield).
Stone was second, with Henderson (Worthing and District S.C.), third. Our boys were in the same position, except Paul, who was having trouble and had dropped a few places.
Henderson, winner of the London—Brighton and Back Walk earlier in the season, walked steadily throughout to finish second.
Henderson, after taking the lead from Sutton, went well ahead and it seemed impossible to catch him. He was pegged back, however, and the leadership was continually changing.
